Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

energyRt 0.90.0 (pre-release)

The first release since 0.50-beta, consolidating the unreleased 0.60-0.80 cycles. The modelling API is the one planned for 1.0; testing and debugging continue. Upgrading from 0.50 is not a drop-in: see Breaking changes.

License

  • The per-object timeslice maps (mTechTimeslice and its siblings, mCommTimeslice, mWeatherTimeslice), the technology activity and output domains (mvTechAct, mvTechOut), meqTechActSng and the availability-factor maps (meqTechAfLo, meqTechAfUp, meqTechAfFx, where the bound is one number per technology, region and year) are defined by a rule, the join of the small tables they are made of, and their tables are dropped at the end of interpolate_model(). Readers see the same tuples; the multimod route enumerates the rule itself and the saved scenario no longer carries the tables. The output and single-output domains keep their tables in a model with coarse processes. options(energyRt.map_rules = FALSE) keeps every table; options(energyRt.map_rules_verify = TRUE) checks each rule against the table it replaces. The availability-factor maps are decided per technology, region and year and recorded as rules without building their tables, in a sparse, unfolded interpolation; a full-year one-country model builds them about 3.5 times faster, with a quarter less peak memory.
  • Relicensed from AGPL-3 to Apache-2.0. Releases up to v0.89 remain AGPL-3.

New features

Model building

  • Three-part storage: charger, reservoir and discharger with their own capacities, costs and availability, coupled by @duration, @inp2out and @inp2stg.
  • Vintages (@vintage) and clusters (@cluster) expand a process into variants at interpolation; getVariants() lists them.
  • Resource tiers: a commodity or weather object with @cluster gets one balance per tier.
  • Weather transforms derive many series from one, and a weather object may be declared at a coarser region than the processes reading it.
  • Transmission: newACLine(), newDCLink(), an optional Kirchhoff voltage law, loss tranches (lossTranches()), route ratings (@trade$af), route ratings over a parent timeslice (@trade$afs) and weather factors of the ratings (@weather, read at the route’s source region).
  • Supply, import and export curves: asSupplyCurve(), asImportCurve(), asExportCurve().
  • Taxes and subsidies are indexed by instrument and can be levied on processes. cap and ncap charge technologies and trades (a trade in each region the levy is placed in); a storage’s capacity is levied by part with stg.cap/stg.ncap (reservoir), inp.cap/inp.ncap (charger) and out.cap/out.ncap (discharger).
  • commodity@property for physical properties; discount rates at any geoscale level; a WACC per technology with payback as its cost-recovery life.
  • Portable process definitions: process_to_spec() / process_from_spec() (YAML/JSON), process_designer(), read_technology_xlsx() / write_technology_xlsx().

Time and space

  • Calendars from timescales, including irregular calendars (months of 28-31 days), sampled calendars (representative days) and the new m12_d365_h24 and m12_d365_h24_1dpm.
  • Multi-level geography from geoscales: commodities and processes may sit at a coarser @geoframe than the flows they touch, with auxiliary flows held in the finer cells beneath.
  • Region aggregation with clustering: aggregate_model_regions(clusters = ), get_process_groups(), process_cluster_sweep(), model_clusters().
  • Sub-territory solves from a filtered geoscale, and subset_model_regions().
  • Auxiliary flows sit at the auxiliary commodity’s timeframe: an annual emission is one variable per year, not one per hour.

Solving

  • Solve drivers: solve_myopic(), solve_by_sample(), solve_by_region() and solve_guided().

  • First-order LP solvers (cuOpt, HiGHS PDLP), and lang = "mm", which builds the problem matrix with multimod. Remote solving on the NEOS server and on cloud GPUs.

  • Matrix presets (backend = "mm") are solved by multimod::solve_mps(): HiGHS in the R session or through Julia, cuOpt on a local GPU through WSL (mm_cuopt_wsl) or on a rented GPU (mm_cuopt_cloud, pyomo_cuopt_cloud).

  • On the lang = "mm" route the activity and output definitions (eqTechAfFx, eqTechActSng) and the per-process totals (eqTechOutTot, eqTechInpTot, the storage, supply, import, export and demand totals) are substituted while the matrix is built: their rows and the columns they define are not written, which reduces a full-year model several-fold. The preset field substitute names the equations; character() builds every row. With a multimod that composes roll-ups, the commodity output and input totals (eqOutTot, eqInpTot) are substituted too.

  • The matrix route removes model.mps (and its compressed copy) once the solution is decoded; the index tables and the solution file stay. The preset field keep_mps = TRUE keeps it. A preset’s mm_solver and where choose the solver and the place. A Pyomo- or JuMP-written matrix carries index tables (from Pyomo’s symbol map, from JuMP’s containers) and is decoded by multimod like its own; julia_mps writes the JuMP matrix and julia_cuopt_cloud solves it on a rented GPU.

  • interpolate_model() is about 6x faster on large models; fx_equ = TRUE writes fixed bounds as single equality rows (about 25% fewer rows on hourly VRE models).

  • MPS output (solver_options$pyomo_mps), read_solution() for solutions produced elsewhere, and en_check_solve(), en_check_packages(), en_install_deps(), en_install_julia_pkgs() to check and set up the toolchains.

  • interpolate_model(model, ..., base = REF) builds a scenario on an interpolated base when the objects added are constraints, cost terms, taxes or subsidies: only what they add is computed, the base’s tables are reused and its store is never written to, and the result equals a full interpolation. Anything else is interpolated in full, with a message saying why. The saved scenario names its base in scenario.yml.

  • A scenario keeps the model as given in @model: the variants, tiers and transform clones interpolation builds are rebuilt when a reader needs them. A saved scenario references its sealed model instead of copying it, also for models with vintages, clusters or a spatial sample. getObject() on a scenario returns the objects as defined.

  • save_dataset(rehash = FALSE) and save_dataset(overwrite = TRUE) stop when another store entry references the version they would rewrite, and name the dependents.

  • base = REF also takes new processes, commodities and other model objects: the per-object tables of the objects REF holds are reused and every map is rebuilt.

  • base = REF takes a sample of REF’s calendar or regions (a calendar of some of its timeslices, a filtered geoscale with boundary_prices): REF’s tables are reused filtered to the sample. Saved, such a scenario references the sealed REF’s tables through a row filter.

Results and project management

  • A project registry keyed on path, with a lifecycle (seal_*(), mark_delete(), …); objects are reachable by name (getScenario("base")).
  • Runs and artifacts: scenario_runs(), scenario_solutions(), promote_solution(), import_solution(), drop_scenario_run().
  • Results in Arrow stores, readable when larger than memory; getData(run = ) reads several runs at once.
  • prepare_for_sharing() and strip_user_info().
  • The dataset store keeps versions by content under one name (datasets/<name>/<hash>/): saving other content under a name adds a version instead of overwriting, load_dataset(name, hash = ) pins one, and the registry lists every version. A references table beside the registry records which scenario points at which version.
  • save_scenario() keeps a scenario’s large interpolated tables (numeric parameters, bounds and maps from energyRt.param_ref_min_rows rows, 1e6 by default; weather and demand series from energyRt.ondisk_min_rows) in its own store and records their hashes in scenario.yml. A scenario built with interpolate_model(base = ) on a saved and sealed base references every table identical to the base’s instead of storing a copy, and keeps the rest. load_scenario() resolves the references; the lazy readers follow them; a writer that changes a table drops its reference. unseal_scenario() refuses while scenarios reference the base’s tables (force = TRUE to unseal anyway). References into the dataset store held by scenarios saved earlier still load; a weather or demand table whose version is gone is recomputed from the model.
  • A scenario seals its inputs and its outputs separately: seal_scenario(x, inputs = TRUE, outputs = FALSE). With sealed inputs and open outputs it can still be solved under a new run label; save_scenario() then writes that run only, so scenarios built on it keep reading the same tables. unseal_scenario(x, inputs = FALSE, outputs = TRUE) reopens the runs alone. A scenario sealed before reads as both parts sealed.
  • save_model() and save_scenario() take mode = "ref" (default, options(energyRt.save_mode)) or "full". "ref" references a repository or model only when its exact content is a SEALED version, and copies it in otherwise; "full" copies everything in. save_scenario() no longer stores an unsealed model in the model store to reference it. Changed: a scenario whose model is stored but not sealed now carries its own copy.
  • A scenario whose model is a sealed version plus repositories added by interpolate_model() references the sealed version and keeps only the added repositories (model: added in its manifest); load_scenario() adds them back.
  • list_versions() lists the versions of models, repositories and datasets with a status (current, in use, marked, unused), when they were sealed, how many entries reference them and their size (details = TRUE for more). mark_delete(version = ) marks superseded versions (sealed ones of models and repositories; a hash, or "unused"), and delete_marked() deletes them when still unreferenced. delete_marked() also keeps an entry while any of its sealed versions has a dependent.
  • list_dependents() replaces store_dependents(): the verified dependents recorded on sealed versions (with recursive = TRUE, transitively) plus the references found in manifests; prune = TRUE drops stale records.
  • Unsealed saves of models and repositories record a save id instead of a content hash (hashed: false in the manifest), so saving a large model no longer serializes it for hashing. The content hash is computed when a decision needs it: saving onto a sealed entry, comparing with the sealed versions of a name, and sealing (which now loads and hashes the payload). An identical re-save of an unsealed entry is written again. options(energyRt.lazy_hash = FALSE) hashes every save.
  • A model whose repository holds unchanged objects of one sealed repository version (taken with getObject() from a loaded sealed repository) references that version with the object names and the hash of the selected objects, verified by load_model(). Sealing a repository records each object’s hash for this.
  • Sealing a model or repository freezes its content as a version (<entry>/<hash>/): unsealed saves update the entry in place and leave the sealed versions untouched, and references and load_*(hash = ) reach a sealed version exactly. A sealed version records the models and scenarios that reference it, and unseal_model() / unseal_repository() list them and refuse while they exist unless force = TRUE.
  • Referenced tables read back into memory are dropped before the scenario shell (scen.RData) is written. A shell above options(energyRt.shell_max_mb = 256) warns and names its largest slots.
  • The mm route no longer copies the scenario’s tables into the multimod model: multimod reads them from the scenario’s store or the dataset store as the matrix is built (multimod_from_energyRt(inMemory = FALSE)), a table held in memory is attached rather than dropped, and the memo size is the preset’s data_cache_gb (32 by default). Once the matrix is written, the model, the memo and the scenario’s tables that are persisted on disk or in the store are released, so a solve, local or in the cloud, waits with the memory free.

Validation and comparison

  • validate_scenario_parameters() (structural versus advisory findings), verify_solution() with check groups, audit_coefficients().
  • compare_scenarios(), compare_models(), compare_inputs().

Reporting and visualisation

  • report() for every class and for models and scenarios (HTML, PDF, Word, TeX), with spatial and solved context (geoscale =, model =, scenario =).
  • levcost(): analytic levelized cost of technologies, storage (LCOS) and trade (LCOT) per vintage, cluster and region; ex-post per variant on a solved scenario.
  • draw() process diagrams; autoplot() for objects, calendars, horizons, scenarios and comparisons; plot_map(), plot_trade_map(), plot_trade_network().
  • TOPIA, the teaching model (was UTOPIA), rebuilt around concentrated resources traded between zones.

Breaking changes

  • slice is timeslice, and a calendar is required; the tsl2*() helpers moved to timescales.
  • Storage: vStorageStore is vStorageLevel; @cap2stg, @charge and @inflow are refused (use @duration, @startLevel or a supply); flows are bounded by converter capacity (inp.af.up / out.af.up default to 1).
  • technology@aeff no longer takes stg2ainp, stg2aout, sinp2ainp, sinp2aout, sout2ainp or sout2aout; they were never read for a technology. A storage’s own @aeff keeps its couplings.
  • @start, @end and @olife are merged into @vintage; vintage and cluster labels must be declared.
  • @geolevel is @geoframe, and a model carries a Geoscale.
  • Taxes and subsidies are indexed by instrument; newConstraintS() and newSub() are removed.
  • Storage auxiliary couplings are part-prefixed (inp.cap2ainp, …).
  • The first argument is object in 66 functions; the scenario API is verb-first (save_scenario(), load_scenario(), …) with en_registry; 46 helpers are no longer exported; the 0.5-era deprecations are removed.
  • The Julia and Python backends exchange Arrow files (Arrow.jl, pyarrow); arrow_format is split into storage_format and exchange_format.
  • UTOPIA is TOPIA (regions W1/W2, C1-C6, E1-E3); the test tier nightly is full.
  • The cloud presets are renamed: mmcloud is mm_cuopt_cloud, mmcloud_crossover is mm_cuopt_cloud_crossover, mmcloud_pyomo is pyomo_cuopt_cloud, mmcloud_pyomo_crossover is pyomo_cuopt_cloud_crossover; a solve with a former name stops and names its replacement. mm_engine is replaced by mm_solver and where; settings stored by earlier versions are still read.
  • get_hf_token() and set_hf_token() are removed: use mmcloud::get_hf_token() and mmcloud::set_hf_token().

Bug fixes

  • A reloaded solve_by_region() sequence served every variant the FIRST unit’s model. The scenario stored the model it was interpolated from, which the driver had already cut, while @model lives on the shell and is written only on the first save – so region R2’s results came back beside a model declaring R1, whose own R2 rows were empty. verify_solution() re-derives identities from that model, and levcost() and report() read its declarations. The driver now stores the full model with each unit’s region set, and the cut is rebuilt per variant.

  • solve_by_region() accepted overlapping group = entries, or a repeated region in regions =, and solved and counted that region twice – including in the “sum of objectives” its print method presents as the whole-system cost. Overlaps are refused, naming the regions.

  • sample_summary()’s mean is weighted by each sample’s year_fraction. Samples need not cover equal shares of the year – method = "sequential" folds a trailing singleton block into its predecessor – and the mean previously gave a larger block the same single vote. The quantiles remain unweighted, and a message says so when coverage varies.

  • subset_model_regions() clears the parent’s recorded content hash. The subset keeps the model’s name on purpose and save_model() updates an entry in place by name, so saving one could overwrite the full model’s store entry.

  • read_sequence() no longer reports a by_region sequence as complete while returning its boundary stub counts as NA; they are declared missing.

  • A spatial sample survives a variant switch: the problem cartridge records it, where before only the shell held it and a reload restored another unit’s regions.

  • A filtered geoscale announces the sub-territory solve unconditionally. The mode is accepted silently, so a geoscale covering only some declared regions used to yield a smaller solve – a different answer from the full model’s – with nothing said unless verbose.

  • About 130 fixes, most of which change results: unwired parameters now reach the solver, equations are no longer instantiated without data, waf.fx binds from both sides, aeff$cout2ainp / cinp2aout bind, sub-region emissions are counted, coarse supply keeps its cost, and get_process_*(process = ) is honoured.

  • A tax or subsidy without @region charged the coarse regions of a geoscale too, i.e. the roll-up of their sub-regions a second time. A commodity rate now applies at the commodity’s own regions and a process rate at the regions the process is declared in; a region off that level is an error.

  • levcost() of a storage sized a charger with no inp2out or inp2stg like the discharger, and a discharger with no duration at one hour of storage. Each is now sized by its own flow, as in the solved model.

  • Auxiliary flows (aeff) of a process were lost when it gave the coefficient for all timeslices and another process gave the same coefficient for named timeslices.

  • Capacity taxes and subsidies on a storage charged nothing unless it had discharger data. They are now levied by part (see above); a levy that selects storages and sets only cap/ncap is an error.

  • A bound declared per region on one object and for all regions on another lost the second object’s bound equation (e.g. a fixed storage duration).

  • Content hashes of models with a geoscale are stable between R sessions (the S7 class object was hashed), so such models match their sealed versions in a new session.

Documentation

  • A rebuilt pkgdown site with tutorial articles, and a runnable example on every public help page.
  • The testing strategy (tiers, the @covers matrix, goldens) is documented in tests/README.md and tests/TESTING.md.

energyRt 0.50.9-dev

Breaking changes

  • Time-slice weighting is rewritten: variables with a slice dimension are no longer weighted, for consistency between sampled and non-sampled runs. Slice weights can vary across model years.
  • Variables with a year dimension are no longer weighted to interval lengths, except cumulative variables (vSupReserveCum) and capacity variables, which represent the state at the end of the period.
  • New-capacity variables (vTechNewCap) are given per year — apply pPeriodLen to get total new capacity by the end of each period.
  • System costs are regrouped by type (capital, fixed O&M, variable O&M, supply, taxes, subsidies) and by process type, and the Total Costs equation rewritten to match.

Bug fixes

  • optimizeRetirment = TRUE no longer retires new technologies at the same time as their installation.
  • draw() on a trade no longer repeats arrows.
  • newCosts() is debugged, with an example in the Topia tutorial.
  • tsl2hour() identifies n-digit hours; it previously worked for two only.
